title: OK Started as a Joke About Bad Spelling
hook: OK began as a joke, spelled wrong on purpose
summary: OK is a joke misspelling of all correct as oll korrect that survived by riding an election slogan.

text: You've probably said OK a few times today.
But these two letters started out as a joke.
Summer 1838, Boston.
A strange fad was spreading through the newspapers.
It was a game of shortening phrases to initials
and even misspelling them on purpose.

panels.mean: oll wright, as in all right
gone to Texas, meaning they took off

panels.text: Newspapers were cracking jokes back then too

text: March 23, 1839, the Boston Morning Post.
It ran o.k. there.
It was short for all correct, misspelled as oll korrect.

panels.text: They misspelled all correct on purpose?

text: Most of these joke words died out fast.
OK survived thanks to this man.
Martin Van Buren, the 8th US president.
His hometown was Kinderhook, so his nickname was Old Kinderhook.
In the 1840 election, his supporters pushed OK as short for that nickname.
Vote for OK. OK gets my vote.
That election got the whole country buzzing.
Van Buren lost it.
The winner was OK.

panels.text: The president lost and the slang stayed

text: This story came out in the 1960s.
Linguist Allen Walker Read
dug it up by searching old newspapers page by page.
